validity.researcher_notes: The row exists and is real (FERC Docket No. CP18-89-000, 'Empire North Project'), but its recorded LengthKnown=40.20 km (25 mi) and Diameter=26.00 in do not match any physical pipe FERC or the operator describes for this project -- the project built ZERO new mainline pipe. Five independent-of-each-other documents agree on the facility list: (1) FERC's own Notice of Intent to Prepare an EA (Federal Register 2018-07924, filed/opened Feb. 16, 2018): 'The Empire North Project would consist of the following facilities: A new 21,000 horsepower (hp) compressor station in Jackson Township, Tioga County, Pennsylvania; a new 32,000 hp compressor station in the Town of Farmington, Ontario County, New York; modifications of the existing regulator valves and station piping and installation of metering facilities at the existing New Victor Regulator Station...; minor modifications to the existing Jackson Meter and Regulator Station...; and upgrading the maximum allowable operating pressure of the Empire Connector Pipeline (ECP) from 1,290 psig to 1,440 psig. The ECP is an existing 76.6-mile-long, 24-inch-diameter pipeline that runs from Victor, New York to Corning, New York' -- i.e. the only pipe named is a DIFFERENT, already-existing, already-counted (on the Main Line row, P0288) segment with a different length (76.6 mi, not 25) and different diameter (24 in, not 26), in a different state (wholly within New York, not PA-to-Ontario). Total land disturbance for the whole project is stated as 50.4 acres -- consistent with two compressor-station sites, not with 25 miles of new linear pipeline construction (which would run to hundreds of acres of temporary ROW). (2) National Fuel's own official 'Empire North Project Fact Sheet' PDF (nationalfuel.com): the facilities list is two new compressor stations + two 'minor modifications' to existing stations + an MAOP uprate on the existing ECP explicitly noted as 'not expected to require any construction-related activities' -- no pipeline mileage anywhere in the facility list. (3) National Fuel's own SEC 8-K investor-presentation exhibit (2019, EDGAR accession 0001193125-19-280494) states outright: 'No new pipeline construction' -- the company's own securities filing, under legal disclosure obligations, using that exact phrase; infrastructure is described as '2 new compressor stations in NY (1) & Pa. (1)'. (4) National Fuel's own current, FERC-effective Empire Pipeline Gas Tariff (effective Sept. 15, 2020, and still governing rates as of the version searched) defines, at Section 1.19 of its General Terms and Conditions: '"Empire North Capacity" shall mean firm transportation capacity resulting from Transporter's incremental facility expansion project authorized in Commission Docket No. CP18-89-000' -- the tariff's own vocabulary treats 'Empire North' purely as a CAPACITY product (paired with an 'Empire North Compressor Fuel Retention' percentage), never as a named physical pipeline segment, in contrast to how the same tariff names the 'Original Empire Pipeline' and the 'Empire Connector' as actual physical assets. (5) A peer deep-sweep shard on this same wiki page's other GEM row (P0288, Empire Pipeline Main Line, in this same batch) independently reached the identical conclusion from its own research and flagged it as a cross-row lead for this exact row, quoting nationalfuel.com's current 'About Empire Pipeline' page: 'In 2020 Empire placed the Empire North Project into service, which saw the construction of two new compressor stations...' with no mention of new pipe. The apparent origin of the erroneous 40.2 km/26 in figures: RBN Energy's project data card for 'Empire North Expansion' (archived, since the live page 403s bots) lists 'Diameter: 26 inches' and 'Length: 25 miles' alongside Origin: Jackson, PA and Destination: Chippawa, ON -- these numbers match the sheet's LengthKnown/Diameter EXACTLY, strongly suggesting RBN Energy's card (via gem.wiki's citation of it) is the sheet's source, and RBN's card appears to describe the general PA-to-Ontario corridor over which the new/uprated capacity flows, not the footprint of new construction. Per this sweep's own standing convention (already applied in this same batch to Rockies Express Zone 3 East-to-West, and to the len-0 Rover phases/Vector P3202): an expansion project that adds capacity via compression/reversal with no new mainline pipe gets LengthKnown=0, Diameter blank -- that convention applies squarely here. Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, StartYear1=2020, and the PA/Ontario endpoints are all independently confirmed (see fills[] below) and are NOT in question -- only the physical Length/Diameter attribution is wrong.

validity.researcher_notes: Everything else about the row is confirmed. Existence: the project is extensively documented -- FERC Docket CP18-89-000 (application filed Feb. 16, 2018; certificate issued Jan. 2019; Federal Register notices in 2018 and 2022), SEC 8-Ks, National Fuel's own fact sheet and tariff, and a third-party industry data card (RBN Energy). This is a real, FERC-certificated, in-service project -- no existence or classification concern. Operator/Owner: 'Empire Pipeline' (Empire Pipeline, Inc.) is independently confirmed as the 100% owner/operator by (1) RBN Energy's data card ('Operator: Empire Pipeline') and (2) National Fuel's own 'About Empire Pipeline' page ('Empire Pipeline, Inc. ... is one of two FERC-regulated subsidiaries of National Fuel Gas Company') -- two independent sources agreeing with the existing Owner1='Empire Pipeline'/100%. Status=operating and Fuel=Gas confirmed by all sources read (RBN: Stage 'Operational'; National Fuel's current page: system is in active service). StartYear1=2020 is confirmed by THREE independent sources that agree with each other over the ORIGINAL 2018 filing's more optimistic schedule: RBN Energy ('In Service Date: Q3/2020'), National Fuel's own SEC 8-K investor deck ('second half of fiscal 2020', NFG's fiscal year runs Oct-Sept, so Apr-Sept 2020), and National Fuel's current 'About Empire Pipeline' page ('completed in 2020'). The project's own 2018-vintage Fact Sheet PDF proposed timeline had targeted November 2019 for in-service -- the ~10-month slip to 2020 is corroborated across three sources independent of that original proposed schedule, so 2020 (not 2019) is the correct StartYear1. Capacity=300.00 MMcf/d matches RBN Energy's card exactly ('Total Capacity: 300 MMcf/d') -- one strong, named-project-specific source; FERC's own certificate order and the tariff describe the INCREMENTAL firm capacity added as 205,000 Dth/d (175,000 Dth/d to the Chippawa/TCPL interconnect + 30,000 Dth/d to the Hopewell/TGP interconnect, per National Fuel's own SEC 8-K deck), which is a materially different (smaller) number than 300 MMcf/d. I could not fully reconcile 300 vs. 205 in the time available -- it may be that 300 MMcf/d is a rounded/total corridor figure inclusive of pre-existing capacity on the reversed path rather than the incremental amount, but I flag this as an open discrepancy for Update rather than silently accepting RBN's number as proven; it does not rise to a 'concern' on its own because RBN's card is a genuine third-party industry-tracking source naming this specific project, but a second source stating 300 (not 205) specifically was not found. SegmentCost=$141,000,000 matches RBN Energy's card exactly ('Est Capital Cost: $141 Million'); National Fuel's own Fact Sheet states '$143 million' and its SEC 8-K deck states '~$145 million' -- three sources within a $4M/~3% band of each other (plausibly different cost-estimate vintages through the project's life: initial filing vs. later updates), so $141M is corroborated as being in the right range from an independent source (RBN) even though it is not the exact figure in National Fuel's own later disclosures; staged as REFS_ADDED at medium tier given the spread. Location: StartState/Province=Pennsylvania and EndState/Province=Ontario/EndCountryOrArea=Canada are confirmed by RBN ('Origin: Jackson, PA'; 'Destination: Chippawa, ON') and independently by the FERC EA notice (naming the Jackson Township, Tioga County, PA compressor station) and National Fuel's SEC deck (naming the Chippawa/TCPL interconnect as a delivery point) -- three independent sources agree.

fills.researcher_notes: Staged at medium, not high: only ONE source (RBN Energy) states 300 MMcf/d specifically for this project; the second source I found, National Fuel's own SEC 8-K investor deck, instead states the certificated INCREMENTAL capacity as 205,000 Dth/d (175,000 Dth/d to the Chippawa/TCPL interconnect + 30,000 Dth/d to the Hopewell/TGP interconnect) -- a different number, likely because it measures incremental added capacity rather than a total/rounded corridor figure. I did not find a second source stating 300 MMcf/d itself, so the second-source search came up short of an exact match rather than empty; flagged in the sibling validity note as an open reconciliation item rather than silently treated as resolved.

The only MAOP figure found in connection with this project (1,290 to 1,440 psig) is explicitly the Empire Connector Pipeline's (ECP) uprate -- FERC's EA notice and the operator's own fact sheet both attribute it to the ECP, a separate, already-existing 76.6-mile/24-in pipe (Victor NY to Corning NY), not to whatever this row is meant to represent (the PA-Ontario 'North Expansion' corridor). Given the Length/Diameter concern staged above -- this row may not correspond to a discrete physical segment at all -- applying the ECP's pressure figure here would compound the same misattribution, so left UNRESOLVED rather than forced.

No source read explicitly names the upstream supply basin for the Empire North reversal capacity specifically. It is plausible this capacity is intended to move Marcellus/Utica-basin gas northward (the reversal flows from Jackson, PA -- Appalachian-basin territory -- to the Chippawa/Ontario border), consistent with National Fuel's 'About Empire Pipeline' page describing the broader system's expansions as enabling delivery of 'less expensive Marcellus gas supplies,' but that page discusses the system generally, not this project's receipt points specifically, so I have not staged an inference as a sourced value. Left UNRESOLVED; next step would be an NFG 10-K/10-Q EDGAR full-text search naming Empire North's specific receipt points.

summary: P2531 (Empire North Expansion) exists and is correctly classified/operated/owned, but LengthKnown=40.2 km and Diameter=26 in are wrong (concern, spec, contested) -- FERC's own EA notice, National Fuel's fact sheet, National Fuel's SEC 8-K ('No new pipeline construction'), and National Fuel's own effective FERC tariff (Sec. 1.19: 'Empire North Capacity' is a firm-capacity product, not a physical segment) all agree this is a compression-only expansion (two new compressor stations) with zero new pipe; recommend LengthKnown=0/Diameter blank per the sweep's expansion-with-no-new-pipe convention. Status/Fuel/StartYear1(2020)/Location/Owner/Operator refs added at high tier; Capacity(300 MMcf/d) and SegmentCost($141M) refs added at medium tier (single strong source each, with a noted discrepancy against National Fuel's own 205,000 Dth/d incremental-capacity and $143-145M cost figures). UNRESOLVED: ConstructionYear (only a superseded 'proposed' Feb. 2019 date found; actual start uncertain given the ~10-month in-service slip), Pressure (only figure found belongs to the unrelated Empire Connector segment), FuelSource (no source names this project's specific receipt-point gas source).
